# Kawi

> Kawi is a regulated Brazilian company that runs a hybrid settlement engine for cross-border payments: local fiat rails such as PIX to enter, Solana and USDC to settle, delivered in the destination currency as one auditable operation.

## Pages
- [Kawi | Hybrid BRL to USDC Settlement Engine for Latin America](https://kawiservices.com.br): Kawi runs a hybrid settlement engine: PIX and local fiat rails for access, Solana and USDC for movement, in one programmable, auditable operation.
- [About Kawi | Hybrid Settlement Infrastructure](https://kawiservices.com.br/about): Who Kawi is: a regulated Brazilian company building hybrid settlement infrastructure that moves value across Latin America in minutes, not days.
- [Blog | Hybrid Settlement, Solana and Payment Economics](https://kawiservices.com.br/blog): Notes from the Kawi team on hybrid settlement infrastructure, Solana as a settlement layer, the economics of prefunding, and agentic payments.
- [Regulation and Compliance: Regulated in Brazil](https://kawiservices.com.br/regulation): Kawi is a regulated company in Brazil and is actively strengthening its regulatory framework for digital assets.
- [Privacy Policy](https://kawiservices.com.br/privacy): Kawi protects user privacy and does not collect personal information without requesting authorization first.
- [Cookies Policy](https://kawiservices.com.br/cookies): Kawi uses cookies and browser storage to keep the site working, remember your preferences and understand how the platform is used.
- [Account Deletion Requests](https://kawiservices.com.br/account-deletion): Users can request account deletion and Kawi will guide the process according to security, compliance and operational requirements.
- [Data Deletion Requests](https://kawiservices.com.br/data-deletion): Users can request deletion of personal data that Kawi no longer needs to provide, secure or legally maintain the service.

## Blog
- [Hybrid Settlement Infrastructure: Fiat and Blockchain](https://kawiservices.com.br/blog/hybrid-settlement-infrastructure): A guide to hybrid settlement infrastructure: how fiat entry rails, stablecoin conversion and blockchain settlement become one auditable operation.
- [Prefunding Strategy for Instant Cross-Border Settlement](https://kawiservices.com.br/blog/prefunding-strategy): Kawi prefunding strategy for instant settlement: pooled stablecoin liquidity, corridor buffers, replenishment triggers and stress reserves.
- [The Economics of Cross-Border Settlement](https://kawiservices.com.br/blog/economics-of-cross-border-settlement): A structural breakdown of cross-border payment costs: intermediary hops, trapped capital, FX spread and overhead, and which of them hybrid settlement removes.
- [Why Solana for Cross-Border Settlement](https://kawiservices.com.br/blog/why-solana-for-settlement): Why Kawi settles cross-border payments on Solana: sub-second block times, fees that stay negligible for small tickets, and deep USDC liquidity.
- [The Kawi Agentic Layer for Settlement](https://kawiservices.com.br/blog/kawi-agentic-layer): The Kawi agentic layer: why autonomous software needs machine-readable quotes, bounded authority, deterministic settlement and verifiable receipts.
- [Hybrid Settlement Benefits for Platforms](https://kawiservices.com.br/blog/benefits-of-hybrid-settlement-for-platforms): The concrete benefits of hybrid settlement for platforms: faster payouts, lower working capital, fewer exceptions and transparent, predictable pricing.
- [Settlement State Machine for Payment Operations](https://kawiservices.com.br/blog/settlement-engine-state-machine): How Kawi models cross-border settlements as an explicit state machine: states, legal transitions, terminal states, compensation and append-only history.
- [Unit Economics of a Cross-Border Settlement](https://kawiservices.com.br/blog/unit-economics-of-a-settlement): A line-by-line unit economics model for a cross-border settlement: network fees, conversion cost, carrying cost of float and contribution margin.
- [Solana Finality and Commitment for Payments](https://kawiservices.com.br/blog/solana-finality-for-payments): How Solana commitment levels work in practice, what confirmed and finalised actually guarantee, and how to choose a waiting policy by ticket size.
- [Primitives for Agentic Payments](https://kawiservices.com.br/blog/primitives-for-agentic-payments): The six primitives autonomous agents need to make payments: verifiable identity, bounded authority, service discovery, machine-readable quotes and receipts.
- [Settlement SLAs and Observability Metrics](https://kawiservices.com.br/blog/settlement-sla-and-observability): Which metrics matter for settlement reliability: percentile completion times, exception rate, break categories and how to define an honest SLA.
- [Fiat Rails vs Blockchain Rails for Payments](https://kawiservices.com.br/blog/fiat-rails-vs-blockchain-rails): A practical comparison of fiat and blockchain payment rails across access, speed, cost, reversibility and auditability, and how hybrid settlement joins them.
- [Spread vs Slippage: The Effective Rate](https://kawiservices.com.br/blog/spread-slippage-and-effective-rate): How to calculate the effective rate of a cross-border settlement: mid-market reference, spread, slippage, fees and the all-in cost customers experience.
- [Solana Fee Economics for Payment Margins](https://kawiservices.com.br/blog/solana-fee-economics): How Solana base fees, priority fees and compute budgets affect settlement cost, why the fee tail matters more than the average, and how to bid well.
- [Machine-Readable Payment Quotes and Intents](https://kawiservices.com.br/blog/machine-readable-quotes-and-intents): How payment quotes should be structured for autonomous agents: intents, itemised costs, explicit expiry, delivered-amount guarantees and signed commitments.
- [Build a Remittance Product on Kawi](https://kawiservices.com.br/blog/building-a-remittance-product-on-kawi): A practical guide to building a remittance product on Kawi: onboarding, quoting the delivered amount, funding, status communication, refunds and support.
- [Idempotency in Payment Systems, in Practice](https://kawiservices.com.br/blog/idempotency-in-settlement-systems): How idempotency keys, deduplication windows and fingerprinting let a payment system guarantee exactly-once settlement on top of at-least-once message delivery.
- [Float and Cost of Capital in Payment Settlement](https://kawiservices.com.br/blog/float-and-cost-of-capital): How to quantify the carrying cost of float in a payments business, why settlement cycle time drives capital efficiency, and how to allocate it per operation.
- [USDC Liquidity on Solana for Settlement](https://kawiservices.com.br/blog/usdc-liquidity-on-solana): Why stablecoin depth matters more than throughput for settlement, how native USDC issuance and redemption reduce risk, and how liquidity caps quotable size.
- [Agent Spend Policies and Payment Guardrails](https://kawiservices.com.br/blog/agent-guardrails-and-spend-policies): How to bound the authority of payment agents: scoped credentials, velocity and amount limits, destination allow-lists, escalation and kill switches.
- [Kawi Widget and API Integration Guide](https://kawiservices.com.br/blog/integrate-the-kawi-widget): How to integrate Kawi: mounting the RaaS widget, driving the same operations from the API, sandbox testing, idempotency keys and webhook handling.
- [Payment Reconciliation by Design](https://kawiservices.com.br/blog/reconciliation-by-design): How to design a settlement system so reconciliation is a lookup, not an investigation: correlation ids, double-entry ledgers and automated matching.
- [Prefunding Inventory Math for Liquidity](https://kawiservices.com.br/blog/prefunding-inventory-math): Applying inventory theory to payment liquidity: safety stock from demand variance, service levels, reorder points and the newsvendor trade-off.
- [Solana Token Extensions for Regulated Flows](https://kawiservices.com.br/blog/token-extensions-for-regulated-flows): How Solana token extensions such as transfer hooks and confidential transfers affect regulated stablecoin settlement, and where policy should stay off-chain.
- [Autonomous Treasury Rebalancing with Agents](https://kawiservices.com.br/blog/autonomous-treasury-rebalancing): How Kawi automates treasury operations with bounded agents: forecasting corridor drain, sizing transfers and operating under hard policy limits.
- [Payment Webhooks: Ordering, Retries, Idempotency](https://kawiservices.com.br/blog/event-driven-settlement-webhooks): How to consume settlement webhooks safely: signature verification, idempotent handlers, out-of-order events, sequence numbers and replay endpoints.
- [Corridor Rebalancing for Payment Liquidity](https://kawiservices.com.br/blog/corridor-rebalancing): How to rebalance liquidity between payment corridors: net flow imbalance, rebalancing versus carrying cost, trigger bands and stablecoin as the medium.
- [Designing Payments for Network Degradation](https://kawiservices.com.br/blog/designing-for-network-degradation): How Kawi handles blockchain congestion: blockhash windows, escalating retries, fee ceilings, backpressure and honest customer communication.
- [Quote Expiry and Price Risk in Cross-Border Settlement](https://kawiservices.com.br/blog/quote-expiry-and-price-risk): Why quote expiry windows exist, how they price the option granted to the payer, and how volatility and funding time determine the right window length.
- [FX Exposure and Hedging in Cross-Border Settlement](https://kawiservices.com.br/blog/fx-exposure-and-hedging): Where FX exposure arises in a settlement flow, how to measure it, and the practical hedging choices: natural offsets, shorter windows and explicit hedges.
- [BRL to USDC: How PIX Becomes Stablecoin](https://kawiservices.com.br/blog/brl-to-usdc-corridor): A step-by-step walkthrough of the Kawi BRL to USDC corridor: quoting, PIX capture, conversion, Solana settlement and delivery, leg by leg.
- [Pricing a Payment Corridor](https://kawiservices.com.br/blog/pricing-a-corridor): A framework for pricing cross-border payment corridors: cost floor, competitive ceiling, risk premium, elasticity by ticket size and transparent pricing.
- [Stablecoins vs Correspondent Banking for Remittances](https://kawiservices.com.br/blog/stablecoins-for-remittances): Why stablecoin settlement outperforms correspondent banking for remittances: fewer hops, distance-independent cost, continuous operation and verifiable records.
- [Settlement Traceability and Security](https://kawiservices.com.br/blog/traceability-and-security): How Kawi makes every settlement verifiable: single correlation ids, append-only state, raw provider evidence and independently checkable on-chain legs.
